title: Beatrix and the Thorn
premise: Edmund Almeida keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in stolen memories, and has spent years making himself unremarkable. When the crown's witch-hunters begin executing anyone with the gift of memory-taking, Edmund discovers that Beatrix, the guild's dying matriarch, hid inside his own mind the sealed memory of the last thorn-king—the spark that once ignited the ancient war between crown and gifted. Hunted by Inquisitor Vane and betrayed by his guild brothers, Edmund must decide whether to destroy the memory or use it to bargain for the gifted's survival. He chooses to release it into the gathered refugees at winter's edge, ending the hunt by making everyone guilty—and beginning a fragile new order with himself as its unwilling archivist.
about_author: Felix Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city he refuses to name. Their fiction blends ledger-precise detail with a thief's tenderness for the things people try to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet him mid-theft, lifting a merchant's first love from her mind and logging it in the Thorn's ledgers. The chapter establishes the guild's economy of impossible things and Edmund's careful invisibility. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as professional pride.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The crown posts its edict: all gifted to be registered, then burned. Guild members scatter or deny their gifts; Edmund burns his own ledger pages but cannot burn what lives in his head. Emotional beat: dread settling like the season's first frost.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Kept
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The dying matriarch reveals she planted something in Edmund years ago—a sealed memory he cannot open—made him promise never to sell it, even to save himself. Emotional beat: the terrible weight of being trusted with someone else's war.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vane Calls on the Thorn
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Vane, himself secretly gifted, offers Edmund immunity in exchange for the guild's remaining stock. Edmund realizes Vane isn't hunting the gift—he's hunting one specific memory. Emotional beat: the sick recognition that invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Brothers of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. His guild brothers vote to hand him over; only the fence Odile helps him flee through the flooded undercity. He learns Beatrix has been taken by Vane's men. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpened by gratitude for one loyal friend.

chapters.title: The Memory That Fights Back
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, intercut with fragments of the sealed memory surfacing: banners, burning orchards, a king crowned in thorns. The seal weakens as winter deepens, and Edmund begins losing hours of himself to it. Emotional beat: horror at becoming a vessel for history.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Captured, Edmund learns Vane was the thorn-king's last soldier, sustained unnaturally for centuries, seeking the memory to finish a war he believes was left unfinished. Emotional beat: pity entangled with fear—an enemy who is also a mourner.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Odile trades her own most precious memory to buy Edmund's freedom and a map to the refugee camps beyond the pass. He must leave her behind, emptied and smiling. Emotional beat: grief as the true price of survival.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the refugee camp, with Vane's forces closing in, Edmund opens the seal fully and finally understands: the memory isn't a weapon but a record of how the last war began—with one side hoarding power and the other refusing to share it. Emotional beat: clarity arriving too late to be comfortable.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Guilty
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Rather than fight Vane, Edmund releases the memory into every mind in the camp, then walks to Vane and takes his centuries of guilt as well. Shared memory ends the hunt: no one can be singled out. Edmund begins a new ledger recording not stolen things, but given ones. Emotional beat: weary, hard-won hope.
